title: Effect of Oral Diamine Oxidase on Symptoms Induced by Histamine Oral Challenge
official: Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial to Evaluate the Effect of Diamine Oxidase (DAO) on the Response to Oral Histamine Challenge
summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether oral diamine oxidase (DAO) can lower symptoms caused by an oral histamine challenge in adults with self-reported food-related histamine symptoms who demonstrate responsiveness to histamine challenge during screening.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 to 65 years.
* History of symptoms after consumption of foods potentially rich in histamine.
* Clinically stable and suitable for oral histamine challenge testing.
* Ability and willingness to provide informed consent.
* Willingness to comply with study procedures and restrictions.
* No clinically relevant medical history.
* No clinically significant findings during screening assessments.
* Positive response to histamine challenge during screening, according to predefined protocol criteria.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Food allergy, celiac disease, peptic ulcer disease, or esophagitis.
* Acute infection.
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
* History of anaphylaxis or severe reactions to histamine.
* Known intolerance to diamine oxidase.
* Severe chronic diseases or medical conditions that may increase risk.
* Excessive alcohol consumption.
* Positive drug or alcohol screening.
* Use of medications that may interfere with histamine or DAO activity.
* Severe reaction during screening histamine challenge.
* Any condition that, in the investigator's opinion, may compromise participant safety or study conduct.
